goal: Make agent-ledger's two linear-time tests tell a quadratic regression from a busy machine, so a red local suite means a real problem (the 1.3.0 release recorded its suite as inconclusive because of them).
changed: test_url_pattern_is_linear_on_dotted_runs and test_a_long_line_of_placeholders_scans_in_linear_time compare CPU time at two sizes 8x apart (tests/helpers.py cpu_growth) and fail above 20x growth, instead of asserting 2 s and 5 s of wall-clock time.

The placeholder test's input adds the policy pattern [A-Z]{8}, which matches inside every placeholder; with built-in patterns only, the old quadratic leftover check ran as fast as the new one, so the test could not catch it.

claims.claim: Both old tests fail on a busy machine with unchanged code.
claims.check: 20 runs of both tests on origin/main while the suite loops in parallel: pass=0 fail=20 at load 109 to 128

claims.claim: Each new test fails on the quadratic code it guards.
claims.check: 20 runs each under suite load with the url_password regex reverted (fail=20, 52x to 60x growth) and with _leftover reverted to the per-character check (fail=20, 53x growth)

claims.claim: Both new tests pass 20 times in a row while the full suite runs in parallel.
claims.check: 20 runs of both tests on Python 3.12 with 8 full-suite loops and 160 busy-loop processes in parallel: pass=20 fail=0, load average 219 at the end
cd tests && python3.12 -m unittest discover -s . (316 tests, OK, 1 skipped)

release.note: Tests only: the linear-time tests for the URL pattern and the placeholder scan now hold on a busy machine, and the placeholder test now reaches the quadratic check it guards.
